evals.prompt: Create a Getting Started page for a developer API product. It should have a brief intro, then use tabs to show installation for Node.js, Python, and cURL.
evals.expected_output: A valid GitBook markdown page with a {% tabs %} block containing three named tabs, each with the appropriate installation command in a code block.
expectations: Output contains a {% tabs %} block with exactly three {% tab %} entries
Each tab has a title matching one of: Node.js, Python, cURL
Each tab contains a fenced code block with the appropriate language tag
Both {% tabs %} and {% tab %} blocks are properly closed with their {% end* %} tags

evals.prompt: Add a warning hint to a page explaining that API keys must never be committed to source control, and a tip hint below it pointing users to environment variable best practices.
evals.expected_output: Two GitBook hint blocks: one with style="warning" about API key security, and one with style="tip" about environment variables.
expectations: Output contains {% hint style="warning" %} block
Output contains {% hint style="tip" %} block
The warning hint mentions API keys and source control
Both hint blocks are closed with {% endhint %}

evals.prompt: Generate a SUMMARY.md for a docs site with three top-level sections: Getting Started (with pages: Quickstart, Installation, Authentication), API Reference (with pages: Overview, Endpoints, Errors), and Changelog.
evals.expected_output: A valid GitBook SUMMARY.md with the correct nested list structure, relative links, and section groupings.
expectations: File contains exactly three top-level sections
Getting Started section has exactly three child pages
API Reference section has exactly three child pages
All links use relative paths ending in .md
Indentation is consistent throughout

evals.prompt: Our CI has a check that fails the build unless every page's `description:` frontmatter value is wrapped in double quotes. It keeps failing on commits GitBook itself pushed through Git Sync. Fix the check.
evals.expected_output: An explanation that GitBook re-serialises `description:` on export in whatever YAML scalar style its serialiser picks (plain, double-quoted, or a `>-` folded block), so a check requiring one style will fight Git Sync. The fix validates that the frontmatter parses and that `description` is non-empty, rather than requiring quotes.
expectations: Identifies that GitBook rewrites `description:` on export and may emit a folded block scalar (`>-`)
Does not simply add `>-` to the list of accepted forms without explaining that the style is not stable
Replaces the style check with a validity check (frontmatter parses, description non-empty)
Keeps the input-side rule intact: hand-written or generated descriptions containing `: ` must still be quoted, or the page imports with an empty description and no error
Does not recommend reverting GitBook's export commits

evals.prompt: Reviewing a Git Sync diff, I see GitBook rewrote some of our cross-space links from https://app.gitbook.com/s/GMqJi8RtGWD6nNlH9QDe/ to https://app.gitbook.com/o/CnvWq8fBYqbTpKXLrLQj/s/GMqJi8RtGWD6nNlH9QDe/. Which form should we standardise on, and should I add a lint rule?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that both forms resolve and neither is canonical: write the short form because that is what GitBook emits in nearly every case, leave the org-qualified form alone where it appears, and add no lint rule for either, because normalising between the two forms churns against Git Sync.
expectations: States that both URL forms resolve and that the org-qualified form is a valid alias, not an error
Recommends writing the short `/s/<spaceId>/<path>` form
Explicitly advises against a lint rule or build step that normalises one form into the other
Does not claim the org-qualified form is the canonical export form
Does not recommend reverting the rewrite
